clues: This city spreads across fourteen islands where a big lake flows out to the sea. It is the biggest city in the far north of Europe.
Summer days here stretch past eighteen hours of light. In late December, days shrink to about six hours, and nights rule the city.
In 1634, this city became the official capital of the empire. New trade rules gave it sole trade rights with foreign merchants.
This island city hosts the Nobel Prize ceremonies each year. Winners then feast at a grand banquet in its city hall.
The leaders who run Sweden work here, in the Rosenbad building. Its parliament sits in the Parliament House too.
